name: Ioi Trade Jargon
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Jones, Alan A. 1998. Towards a lexicogrammar of Mekeo (an Austronesian language of West Central Papua). Pacific Linguistics C-138. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C138
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Phonology/stress statements concern Mekeo proper only (penultimate main stress, secondary every second syllable leftward: pp. 67, 249, 560). The Ioi trade language is mentioned once, p. 8 (p. 28): 'traces of two inland trade languages which contain large quantities of Kunimaipa vocabulary combined with a radically simplified Mekeo grammar (one in Imunga and one in Ioi)'; nothing on its phonology or stress. p. 23 table: Ioi (Mekeo name Aŋabu, pop. 101) is a North Mekeo village.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A., P. Mühlhäusler & D. T. Tryon (eds). 1996. Atlas of languages of intercultural communication in the Pacific, Asia and the Americas, vol. II.1 (text). Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter (ISBN 3-11-013417-9).
sources.note: Print volume containing Jones 1996; not on archive.org).

sources.citation: Jones, Alan Anthony. 1993. Towards a lexicogrammar of Mekeo. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl:1885/133193
sources.note: Same single passing mention of the Ioi and Imunga trade languages (thesis p. 10, p. 39); stress statements are for Mekeo proper; nothing on the trade jargon's phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 languoid ioit1234 and reference 119660 (local CLDF copy andhttps://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/119660)
sources.note: Database record only: classification Pidgin > Mekeo-based pidgin (with imun1234); sole reference Jones 1996, doctype minimal; no phonological content.

sources.citation: Jones, Alan A. 1996. Privately owned Mekeo-based trade languages. In Wurm, Mühlhäusler & Tryon (eds), Atlas of languages of intercultural communication in the Pacific, Asia and the Americas, 219-224. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only published description of the Ioi (and Imunga) trade languages; Glottolog's sole reference and Glottolog's most extensive description. A 6-page atlas entry rated 'minimal'/wordlist-level, so a stress statement is possible but unlikely; it must be opened to settle the question.

sources.citation: Chapter in Hickey, Raymond (ed.) 2020. The Handbook of Language Contact, 2nd ed. Wiley-Blackwell (chapter referring to 'three varieties - Imunga, Ioi, and Maipa' of the Mekeo trading language, per a Google Books record seen in the imun1234 check; chapter/author not identified).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Second-hand survey mention only; would at most restate Jones 1996. Low priority, but the only other known text naming the Ioi variety.
